sources.title: Ops review with warehouse leads 7 Oct

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Morning all. Kicking off the StackYard move from Corvane to Nimbara. This channel is for the boring infra details, war-room is for go/no-go stuff.

units.author: Oleg Sidorenko
units.text: Hi, Oleg here, contractor for the database side. Will be around 10-18 UK time

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Welcome Oleg! Access requests go through me

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Region shortlist on Nimbara: uk-west-2 and uk-south-1. eu-central-1 only as a backup target. Will decide this week

units.text: uk-south-1 was cheaper in their calculator btw

units.author: Marcus Hale
units.text: do we need a new VPN to the warehouses or does the old one just move?

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: new tunnels, the Corvane ones die with the account

units.text: latency from Leeds to uk-south-1 vs uk-west-2, anyone measured?

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: 11ms vs 9ms from the Leeds office, basically the same

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Decision: prod goes in uk-west-2. uk-south-1 is cheaper but has no managed postgres yet, not doing self-managed for this. Backups replicate to eu-central-1.

units.text: quick q — once we're on Nimbara, do the handhelds keep their direct postgres connection? the old firmware image has the db string baked in

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Cutover window: Saturday 17 Oct 2026, 22:00–04:00 UTC. Freeze on StackYard deploys from Thursday 15 Oct.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Scope: StackYard WMS (api, picker web, print service), Postgres primary, BI read replica. Not in scope: Phoenix invoicing (decommissioned separately).

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Target environment: Nimbara uk-west-2, managed Postgres 16.4, 3 app nodes behind the Nimbara load balancer. Backups replicate to eu-central-1.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Roles: Tom (cutover lead), Oleg (database), Jess (application), Marcus (QA), Hannah's shift leads (warehouse checks), Priya (go/no-go).

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Go criteria: replication lag < 5s for the last 72h, smoke tests green on Nimbara staging, all Leeds handhelds on gateway firmware.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Dress rehearsal on staging the weekend before cutover; results logged in #migration-war-room.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: T-24h: announce freeze, confirm on-call, check DNS TTL is 60s, final terraform plan.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: T-1h: stop label print cron, drain queues on Corvane api nodes, notify Leeds night shift.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: 1. Put Corvane api in read-only mode. 2. Wait for replication lag 0. 3. Promote Nimbara primary. 4. Switch DNS. 5. Start api on Nimbara.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Handheld traffic: HTTPS to the api gateway (gw.stackyard.internal) only. Warehouse subnets have no route to the database.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Restart Leeds label printers after DNS switch (printers cache DNS for 30 min).

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Shift leads scan 10 test pallets per site, print 5 labels, run one picklist end to end.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Trigger: any warehouse check fails, or error rate > 2% for 15 min. Steps: 1. Switch DNS back. 2. Take Corvane out of read-only. 3. Replay writes from the Nimbara audit log. Owner: Tom; shift leads confirm handhelds reconnect.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Rollback is possible until 03:00 UTC. After that we fix forward.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Corvane read replica retained for 14 days after cutover as a fallback (decommission T+14).

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Monitoring: error rate, p95 latency of /picklists and /labels, replication off, db CPU.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Comms: Priya posts in #general at start and end. Hannah briefs shift leads.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Phoenix invoicing: last month-end run on Corvane, exports move to the new SFTP. Decommission tracked by Jess.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Open items: Phoenix SFTP exports, BI box connection string, label printing duplicates.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Move StackYard and its database from Corvane Cloud to Nimbara before the Corvane contract ends on 31 Dec 2026.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Target cutover: mid-October, after replication has run stable for at least two weeks.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Wave 1: first site (Leeds or Doncaster, decided at the September sync). Wave 2: Manchester, November, after the retail promo peak.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Biggest risks: handheld firmware, replication lag on stock_movements, cutover during busy periods.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Budget: Nimbara run-rate should stay below current Corvane spend (€9,200/month).

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Out of scope: Phoenix forklift telemetry pilot (ops-owned, separate vendor).

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: OK, let's start. Three things: which site first, Manchester, and fallback.

units.author: Oleg Sidorenko
units.text: Replication status first, quickly: lag is mostly under four seconds, spikes during the two a.m. recount job.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: We're moving that job to five a.m., that should flatten it.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Good. So, first site.

units.author: Hannah Price
units.text: Leeds is the one we care about most, it's the biggest. I'd rather it went first while everyone's fresh.

units.author: Marcus Hale
units.text: Leeds still has older firmware on some handhelds, but we're reflashing.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Then Leeds goes first — but only if replication lag stays under five seconds for seventy-two hours straight. If it doesn't, Doncaster goes first, it's the smaller site.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Works for me.

units.author: Hannah Price
units.text: Fine.

units.author: Oleg Sidorenko
units.text: Seventy-two hours is fine, I will post lag numbers in infra every morning.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Manchester.

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: Manchester is wave two, November, after the promo peak. Different network setup, we don't want to touch it in October.

units.author: Hannah Price
units.text: Agreed, Manchester is chaos in October anyway.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Fallback after cutover?

units.author: Tom Becker
units.text: After cutover we keep the Corvane read replica running for two weeks, so if something is badly wrong we still have the old data live.

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Agreed, two weeks.

units.author: Jess Lindqvist
units.text: While we're here — label printing on a queue, can we squeeze it in?

units.author: Priya Nair
units.text: Let's park that, Tom's not keen. Next item.

units.author: Oleg Sidorenko
units.text: One more: I'll need a bigger instance for the migration week, will ask in billing.

units.text: Thanks everyone.
